strategy.summary: The Python binding helper numpyTypeToCvDepth() in modules/python/src2/cv2_util.cpp lacks a case for NPY_LONG. On Windows (LLP64) numpy int32 is C long, so int32 arrays arrive as NPY_LONG (typenum 7) and are misclassified: pyopencv_to() falls back to the cast-and-copy path, which output arguments reject even though the data is already bit-identical to CV_32S. Reproduce by building the Python bindings at the buggy commit on Windows and running modules/python/test/test_misc.py::test_InputOutputArray (plus test_watershed), which fails there.

input_output_examples.input: On Windows: cv.utils.dumpInputOutputArray(np.zeros((2, 3), dtype=np.int32))
input_output_examples.buggy_output: numpyTypeToCvDepth() has no case for NPY_LONG (typenum 7), so int32 output arrays are routed through the cast-and-copy path; the returned type string does not contain 'type(-1)=CV_32SC1'
input_output_examples.expected_output: Returned string contains 'type(-1)=CV_32SC1'

input_output_examples.input: On Windows: cv.watershed(img, np.int32(markers)) with an int32 output markers array
input_output_examples.buggy_output: cv2.error: (-5:Bad argument) in function 'watershed' Overload resolution failed: - Layout of the output array markers is incompatible with cv::Mat
input_output_examples.expected_output: watershed accepts the int32 markers output array and succeeds

strategy.summary: Reproduce the NaN-bypasses-bounds-check numerical bug in OpenCV ptcloud TSDF integration (PR #29766, issue #29763) at buggy commit 73b7cce6094432d4938860b8e23f50a4913deb5f. A singular cameraPose makes Matx44f::inv() produce NaN coordinates; IEEE 754 makes NaN < 0 and NaN >= limit both false, so the SIMD and scalar bounds checks in integrateTsdfVolumeUnit()/bilinearDepth() let NaN through, causing an out-of-bounds v_load_low() read at tsdf_functions.cpp:181 and SIGSEGV. The new test Volume.issue_29763 exercises this and must crash/fail on the buggy commit and pass (0 points, no crash) once fixed.

input_output_examples.input: volume.integrate(depth, cameraPose) with depth = 256x256 CV_32F filled with 2.0f, K = Matx33f(2.0793828200968182e-21f,0,0, 0,2.0793828200968182e-21f,2.079376761645066e-21f, 0,0,1), singular 4x4 cameraPose from issue #29763 (test_tsdf.cpp Volume.issue_29763), VolumeType::TSDF, resolution 128^3, voxelSize 0.5f, truncate 0.001f, depth factor 1.0f, integrate size 256x256.
input_output_examples.buggy_output: SIGSEGV at v_load_low(row0 + xi) in tsdf_functions.cpp:181 from an out-of-bounds read: NaN passes the bounds check, v_floor(NaN) yields an indefinite integer (INT_MIN on x86 via cvtps_epi32) used as a row/column index; NaN projections may corrupt voxels.
input_output_examples.expected_output: No crash; volume.integrate() completes and volume.fetchPointsNormals(points, normals) returns points.total() == 0u (assertion in test_tsdf.cpp Volume.issue_29763).

strategy.summary: Reproduce a numerical correctness bug in cv::fisheye::calibrate: the automatic focal-length initialization used max(image_size.width,image_size.height)/CV_PI, which makes the image-corner field of view exceed 180 degrees and destabilizes calibration. On the buggy commit b2db9596193857156dbf8406fac77e5a54aa17cf, fisheyeTest.Calibration (and EstimateUncertainties) fail the strict gold K/D assertions; the fix changes the divisor from CV_PI to 2.

input_output_examples.expected_output: Final parameter init becomes Vec2d(max(image_size.width, image_size.height)/2., max(image_size.width, image_size.height)/2.), keeping principal point at Vec2d(image_size.width/2.0 - 0.5, image_size.height/2.0 - 0.5).

strategy.summary: Numerical correctness bug in cv::calibrateHandEye for CALIB_HORAUD (and DANIILIDIS) caused by quaternion sign ambiguity: relative-rotation quaternions qcij with negative real part are used without normalization, corrupting the rotation equations. On issue #24871 data HORAUD returns a rotation error of ~pi (3.139089 / 3.141151) while PARK is ~0.005; DANIILIDIS returns nan and ANDREFF throws. Reproduce by building opencv_test_calib3d and running the PR regression test Calib3d_CalibrateHandEye.regression_24871 at buggy commit cc49aee0.

input_output_examples.input: Issue #24871 reproducer: cv::calibrateHandEye(..., CALIB_HORAUD) on hand-eye rotation-translation pairs with noise.
input_output_examples.buggy_output: HORAUD rotation error 3.139089, translation error 0.000000; PARK rotation error 0.005489; DANIILIDIS returns nan/nan; ANDREFF throws an exception.
input_output_examples.expected_output: HORAUD recovers the true hand-eye transform; rotation error drops to ~0.005 rad (PARK level) with zero translation error.

input_output_examples.input: Issue #24871: same setup without translation and without noise, CALIB_HORAUD selected.
input_output_examples.buggy_output: HORAUD rotation error 3.141151 (PARK rotation error 0.004144); DANIILIDIS nan/nan; ANDREFF exception.
input_output_examples.expected_output: HORAUD rotation estimate agrees with ground truth to within tolerance (not ~pi radians); error at PARK-like ~0.004-0.005 rad level.

input_output_examples.input: Test regression_24871 synthetic data with true X = [[0,0,-1,0.1],[1,0,0,0.2],[0,-1,0,0.3],[0,0,0,1]]; estimate cam2gripper R,t via TSAI, PARK, HORAUD, ANDREFF, DANIILIDIS and compare to ground truth within 1e-9.
input_output_examples.buggy_output: HORAUD (and DANIILIDIS/ANDREFF) do not recover the true cam2gripper R,t; the comparison to ground truth exceeds the 1e-9 tolerance, so the test assertion fails.
input_output_examples.expected_output: Estimated R and t match the ground truth T_true_cam2gripper within the 1e-9 tolerance for TSAI, PARK, HORAUD, ANDREFF and DANIILIDIS.

strategy.summary: Reproduce the CUDA DNN NaryEltwise broadcasting bug (PR #24834) at buggy commit be1373f01a6bcdc40e4a397cfb266338050cc195. input_output_examples.input: YOLOv8n ONNX (yolo detect export model=yolov8n.pt format=onnx opset=12), input Size(640,640), output layer 'output0', run with DNN_BACKEND_CUDA / DNN_TARGET_CUDA, compared against DNN_BACKEND_OPENCV / DNN_TARGET_CPU.
